Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Radwag Zaklad Mechaniki"
- Document: "Radwag Zaklad Mechaniki Precyzyjnej"

The actual company name is "Radwag Wagony Elektroniczne" — well, historically Radwag was "Radwag Zakład Mechaniki Precyzyjnej" (Radwag Precision Mechanics Works). The document's value "Radwag Zaklad Mechaniki Precyzyjnej" is a fuller form — "Zakład Mechaniki Precyzyjnej" = "Precision Mechanics Plant". The register truncated it to "Radwag Zaklad Mechaniki".

So this is not different-entity; it's the same company, with the document carrying the fuller/more complete name. The rules say: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. Here the document value is a superset — the register truncated part of the name. Is that "same-entity"? Yes — clearly the same company. The best value: which one should the fused record carry?

The rules: document-noise → best from register. Different-entity → document's. Same-entity → for number/year format differences, register's canonical form. But for same-entity name drift, what's best? The document is the legal instrument (as stated in different-entity rule rationale). The document's fuller name "Radwag Zaklad Mechaniki Precyzyjnej" is more accurate/complete. I'd pick the document's value as best since it's the more complete form from the legal certificate, and it's not noise.

Verdict: same-entity. Best value: document's fuller form. Why: the register truncated the company name; the certificate carries the full legal name of the same company.

Alternatively, one could argue register canonical form, but the register value looks like a truncation/normalization artifact. The document being the legal instrument, its fuller name is preferable.
